33 The filament of a 240 V, 100 W electric lamp heats up from room temperature to its operating
temperature. As it heats up, its resistance increases by a factor of 16.
What is the resistance of the filament at room temperature?
A
36 Ω
B
580 Ω
C
1.5 kΩ
D
9.2 kΩ

hints: Notice the $240 \, \text{V}$ and $100 \, \text{W}$ ratings apply at the hot operating temperature, not at room temperature.
Recall the power-resistance relation for a fixed voltage $P = V^2/R$ and rearrange it to find the hot filament resistance.
After finding the hot resistance near $580 \, \Omega$, remember the hot value is 16 times larger, so divide by 16 to get the room temperature value.
walkthrough: Identify that $V = 240 \, \text{V}$ and $P = 100 \, \text{W}$ describe the lamp at its operating temperature.
Use electrical power $P = V^2/R_{hot}$ because $V$ and $P$ are known, so $R_{hot} = V^2/P$.
Relate hot to cold: $R_{hot} = 16 \times R_{room}$, so $R_{room} = R_{hot}/16$.
Calculate $R_{room} = 576 \, \Omega / 16 = 36 \, \Omega$, with unit $\Omega$ as required for resistance. This is option A.

A.explanation: The hot resistance is $576 \, \Omega$ from $P=V^2/R$, so the room temperature value is $576/16 = 36 \, \Omega$.

B.explanation: This is the hot operating resistance $R = 240^2/100 = 576 \, \Omega$, before dividing by the factor of 16.

C.explanation: This is too large and does not follow from $R_{hot}=V^2/P$ divided by 16.

D.explanation: This multiplies the hot resistance by 16 instead of dividing, giving about $576 \times 16$.
